concepts.label: node
concepts.gloss: A node is a forwarding domain element in the topology (a physical or logical network device) that contains termination points and participates in links inside a multi-layer topology.
concepts.example: R1 is a node in the OTN-over-optical topology that hosts NEPs such as nep-R1-R2 and participates in links link-R1-R2 and link-R1-R3.

concepts.label: link-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A link-termination-point (LTP or NEP) is a node-owned termination where a link attaches to a node, representing the node-side interface that terminates that link.
concepts.example: nep-R1-R2 is an LTP located on node R1 that terminates link-R1-R2 and provides the attachment point for that inter-node connection.

concepts.label: transitional-link
concepts.gloss: A transitional-link (adaptation link) is a node-local adaptation construct that performs layer mapping or adaptation (multiplexing) of one protocol/tributary into another on a node.
concepts.example: OTU4/ODU2 adaptation at R1 is a transitional-link on node R1 that adapts an ODU2 client stream into OTU4 transport so the ODU2-based connectivity can traverse the optical layer.

concepts.label: service-interface-point
concepts.gloss: A service-interface-point (SIP) is an access point on a node through which a connectivity-service is exposed or consumed (the service-facing interface of a node).
concepts.example: sip-A1-odu is a SIP on node A1 that provides access to the ODU-level connectivity service (for example the service instance cs-a1a3-odu2).

concepts.label: connectivity-service
concepts.gloss: A connectivity-service is an abstract end-to-end service representing a requested connection between service-interface-points; it is carried over a topology, uses SIPs, and is realized by connection end points (CEPs).
concepts.example: cs-a1a3-odu2 is a connectivity-service describing an ODU2 connection from A1 to A3 that uses SIPs (sip-A1-odu, sip-A3-odu) and is realized by CEPs (cep-a1a3-R1, cep-a1a3-R3) across the OTN-over-optical topology.

concepts.label: layer-protocol-qualifier
concepts.gloss: A layer-protocol-qualifier is a descriptor of how one layer protocol is mapped or multiplexed into another (a multiplexing/qualification used to qualify connectivity behavior).
concepts.example: ODU2 mapped into OTU4 is an LPQ indicating that the connectivity service carries ODU2 client traffic encapsulated inside OTU4 transport.

concepts.label: node-rule-group
concepts.gloss: A node-rule-group is a configured grouping of switching or cross-connect rules on a node that defines how traffic is switched or connected inside that node.
concepts.example: R2 cross-connect rule group is a node-rule-group on node R2 that contains the cross-connect rules used to switch incoming ODU channels to the correct outgoing channels for service paths.

concepts.label: link
concepts.gloss: A link is a relationship connecting two nodes in the topology (physical or logical path) that is terminated by LTPs at each end and carries transport between those nodes.
concepts.example: link-R1-R2 is a link between nodes R1 and R2 that is terminated by LTPs (for example nep-R1-R2 on R1 and the corresponding NEP on R2) and carries OTU4 transport between the nodes.

concepts.label: topology
concepts.gloss: A topology (multi-layer topology) is the container object that holds the set of nodes and links (and their inter-layer artifacts) that together define the network domain over which services are provided.
concepts.example: The OTN-over-optical domain is the topology containing nodes R1,R2,R3,A1,A2,A3, links such as link-R1-R2 and link-A1-R1, and adaptations like the OTU4/ODU2 adaptation at R1.

concepts.label: connection-end-point
concepts.gloss: A connection-end-point (CEP) is the node-local endpoint instance that participates in and realizes a connectivity-service; it represents the service's presence at a particular node.
concepts.example: cep-a1a3-R1 is a CEP on node R1 that is part of the realization of cs-a1a3-odu2 and represents the service endpoint of the A1‑to‑A3 ODU2 connection at R1.
